resources.string: The on-screen controller: what each button does, its look, Pro Touch and macros
The controls change by themselves with what the game shows: the fight, the campaign map or the menus. Pick a scene above to see its layout and, further down, what each button does.
In the editor, drag a button to move it; tap it to change its size (− +) and opacity (α− α+), or to hide and show it. Each scene has its own layout.
Game: a button for each action of Ultimate Ninja 5 (attack, jump, chakra, item, guard, Jutsu, Ougi and the specials), with a layout per scene. Classic: the usual PS2 pad.
Fight, campaign or menu controls, changed by themselves as the game goes. Off: the fight ones stay all the time.
Writes the action under each button\'s icon. Off: only the icon and, in the corner, the PS2 button.
Each button shows a drawing of its action. The mark in the corner is the PS2 button it presses, or the sequence it plays in one touch.
Moves the fighter. With Pro Touch it can appear where your thumb lands, on the left of the screen.
Repeated taps make the combo; with a direction, other moves. In clashes, tap fast and repeatedly.
Hold to fill the chakra bar, which the Jutsu and the Ougi spend.
Uses the item picked in the item bar, at the bottom of the screen.
L1 and R1 go to the previous or the next item of the bar.
One touch presses △ then ○: the character\'s jutsu. Spends chakra.
One touch presses △, △ and ○: the ultimate jutsu. It needs chakra and being close, because the hit must land for the scene to start. In the scene, tap the button the game asks for.
One touch plays the game\'s ↑, ↑, ○ input, letting go of the direction between the two ↑. While it plays, the D-pad waits.
Hidden by default: R3 has not been seen doing anything in UN5\'s fights yet. To try it, show it in the layout editor.
Pauses the fight (the game\'s pause menu).
Graphics, controls, layout and quitting the game. Android\'s Back opens the same menu.
Buttons you make in the Macros section below: several buttons together or a sequence in one touch. They appear in fights and in the campaign.
Walks around the map. With the floating stick, put your thumb anywhere on the left side.
Jumps. In a conversation, moves the text on.
The PS2 buttons, doing whatever the game does with them on the map.
Goes back to the previous screen.
Whatever the screen asks: on character select, ○ picks one at random.
On character select, L1 changes the outfit\'s colour.
Starts at the title screen and lets the 2nd player join.

For fast play, against another person or online: your finger slides across every button, the fight\'s D-pad is larger and fixed with a wide touch area, and you set its size, the dead zone and the touch area. Off, the controller is the plain one.
For the game layout, in every scene.

Drag your finger from one button to another and the new one is pressed at once, without lifting: Jutsu, Ougi, specials, macros and L1/R1 included. Off: only between Attack, Jump, Chakra, Item and Guard.
The D-pad stays where you put it in the layout editor. Larger is easier to hit without looking; a touch well around it still counts.
The centre that presses no direction. Larger avoids directions you did not mean; smaller responds earlier.
How much around each button still counts as touching it. Larger forgives imprecise touches.
Each button\'s position, size and opacity, in each scene: in the layout editor.
The on-screen controller\'s gestures and what Pro Touch changes.

With your finger on Attack, slide onto the Jutsu or a special: each button your finger enters is pressed, and the previous one is let go. With Pro Touch it works for every action button, the specials and the macros.

In a fight the D-pad stays in its place, larger than the plain one, and a touch inside the wide box around it lands on it. Once your thumb is on it, it steers in eight directions, diagonals included, even if it slides past the edge.
The middle circle presses no direction. Larger if you rest your thumb, smaller if you want a quick response.
A touch a little outside the button still counts. The size of that margin is set in Pro Touch.
Jutsu, Ougi and specials in one touch
These buttons play the game\'s sequence for you, with the right timing between presses: △ ○ (Jutsu), △ △ ○ (Ougi), ↑ ↑ ○ (Special 1) and ↓ ↓ ○ (Special 2).
A macro is a button of your own: it presses several buttons together or plays a sequence, step by step, with each step\'s time. It can repeat while you hold it (turbo).
Drag any button wherever you like. Tap it to change its size and opacity or to hide it. Each scene (fight, campaign, menus) has its own layout.
A macro is a button of your own on the screen, for fights and the campaign: it presses several buttons at once or plays a sequence, step by step.
The button shows its first 3 letters.

The steps play in order. Each holds the buttons marked for the time chosen; buttons marked in the same step are pressed together. A step with no buttons is a pause. The game reads the pad every 20 ms: use 50 ms or more per step.
Plays again while the button is held (turbo).
In fights and the campaign. Its place is chosen in the layout editor.
